adjudicated_text: ए॒वा ह॑स्य॒ काम्या॒ स्तोम॑ उ॒क्थं च॒ शंस्या॑ । इन्द्रा॑य॒ सोम॑पीतये ॥ ६ ॥
adjudication: Three independent readers agreed EXACTLY on the accent layer: 6 anudatta + 5 svarita = 11, with identical (word_index, aksara_index, type) tuples for all 11 marks (verified programmatically). One aksara identity was disputed: word 1 aksara 0, read HYA by R1, HA by R2, A by R3 - a 1-1-1 split with no majority. ADJUDICATED FROM THE SCAN: (a) the conjunct reading HYA is RULED OUT on width. R1, R2 and R3 each independently measured this aksara at 79-83 px. R2's on-line controls give 82 px for the single consonant CA and 114-120 px for every consonant+YA conjunct on the same line (SYA 114 px, M+YA 120 px), because this fount always writes YA with its own crescent counter and stem. An adjudicator body-band column profile confirms the word occupies x575-783 with the aksara break at ~662-670, i.e. 88 px + 114 px. (b) Between HA and A the 2024 px raster does not settle it. 2 of 3 readers (R1, R2) saw HA-based ink. The adjudicator composited the glyph against a certain A and a certain HA from canvas 32 line 19 (a line already settled by readers Q1/Q2), and found the disputed glyph's left element to be a rounded curl with an inner hook and a down-right tail - the HA structure - rather than the angular two-lobe form of the certain A. HA is adopted as the majority-supported reading with R1's subjoined YA removed on the width evidence. R3's A reading is preserved as recorded dissent and the aksara remains flagged unclear. This locus provably does not affect any gate metric: all three readings yield identical mark tuples, because HYA, HA and A are all a single aksara cluster in position 0.

readers.dissent: Read word 1 aksara 0 as HYA (ha + subjoined ya), from a mid-height left spur on the stem. OVERRULED: 79-83 px is the single-consonant width class on this line; consonant+ya is 114-120 px.
readers.y_bands: Measured by row-ink projection over the whole 3216 px line in leaf-block coordinates (text block = image crop 292,332-3508,5158; block 3216x4826; line 5 body run y 997-1112). readers.boundary_interpretation: WORD BOUNDARIES. I projected column ink over the sirorekha band (y 1031-1044) and over the whole line (y 995-1130). The headline is continuous inside a word and breaks only between words, by 35-49 px. That gives ten word runs plus the tail punctuation, in block-x: 341-534, 575-783, 822-1110, 1149-1383, 1422-1661, 1698-1787, 1828-2065, 2107-2124 (the single danda, only 18 px wide), 2166-2437, 2472-2922; then 2984-3001 and 3007-3025 (a double danda), 3050-3116 (the verse numeral), 3142-3181 (a second double danda). The decisive check is that 2472-2922 is one unbroken 451 px headline covering five aksaras, which proves the 40-49 px breaks are word breaks and not aksara breaks. WORD INDEXING. word_index counts Devanagari words only, left to right: 0 eva, 1 hyasya, 2 kamya, 3 stoma, 4 uktham, 5 ca, 6 shamsya, 7 indraya, 8 somapitaye. The single danda, the double dandas and the numeral are NOT counted as words; if a comparer counts the single danda as a token, add 1 to my indices 7 and 8. AKSARA BOUNDARIES came from a second column projection restricted to the body band y 1050-1126, where aksaras inside a word do separate: eva 348-416 / 428-523; hyasya 580-661 / 670-774; kamya 829-938 / 953-1099; stoma 1158-1291 / 1305-1375; uktham 1430-1495 / 1509-1652; shamsya 1834-1903 / 1912-2053; indraya 2175-2323 (the initial i and the ndra cluster touch at body level) / 2336-2354 (the aa stem) / 2372-2431; somapitaye 2474-2582 / 2586-2665 / 2681-2772 / 2789-2844 / 2859-2917. MARKS NEAR A BOUNDARY, and how I resolved each. (a) svarita x 648 in hyasya sits 13 px inside the first aksara (580-661) and 22 px clear of the second (starts 670), so aksara 0. It stands directly over a stem that continues below the headline at exactly the same x (641-655), and that stem belongs to aksara 0. (b) anudatta x 752 (bar 734-771) lies wholly inside 670-774, aksara 1 of hyasya, 64 px right of the aksara break; unambiguous. (c) anudatta x 1040 (bar 1021-1059) lies wholly inside the second aksara of kamya (953-1099), 68 px right of the break at 938/953; unambiguous. (d) svarita x 1361 (1356-1367) lies inside the ma of stoma (1305-1375), over the right stem of ma, 8 px from its right edge but 55 px from the next word (headline starts 1422); assigned to ma, aksara 1. (e) anudatta x 1479 (bar 1461-1497) is centred under the initial u (1430-1495) and stops 12 px before the next aksara starts at 1509; assigned to u, aksara 0. This is the only bar whose right edge just crosses an aksara break, but its centre and the bulk of its ink sit under u. (f) svarita x 2652 (2646-2658) sits inside the ma of somapitaye (2586-2665), over the right stem of ma, 13 px from its right edge and 23 px before pa starts at 2681; assigned to ma, aksara 1 (so=0, ma=1, pii=2, ta=3, ye=4). (g) in indraya the initial i ends near x 2230 in the rendered glyph, so svarita x 2304 is over the ndra cluster, above its n/d stem: aksara 1. anudatta x 2407 (2389-2426) is wholly inside the final ya (2372-2431): aksara 2. (h) anudatta x 1759 (1741-1778) sits under ca, a one-aksara word (1710-1777): aksara 0. (i) anudatta x 362 (bar 344-380) sits under the initial e (348-416), 48 px before va starts at 428: aksara 0 of eva.
readers.notes: MAGNIFICATION. I started from the two supplied 1568 px segments (about 1:1 with the 2024 px native scan). Because the raster carries no further detail, I then worked mainly by direct measurement of the source image with PIL - row-ink profiles, column-ink profiles and 8-connected component bounding boxes - and used self-rendered LANCZOS crops of the same line at about 2.6x, 5.2-6.0x and 6.45x only to check the SHAPE of each candidate against its measured box. Every x and y quoted is in leaf-block coordinates, which for this line are identical to global line-x: the line spans the full 3216 px block width, so seg1_x/0.9469 and 1560 + seg2_x/0.9469 both recover block-x. ACCEPTED MARKS. Six anudatta: the only components in my bar band y 1134-1146 are 344-380, 734-771, 1021-1059, 1461-1497, 1741-1778 and 2389-2426, all 37-39 px wide and 10-12 px tall, i.e. flat dashes inside the stated 20-45 by 5-18 profile. A 4-pixel-minimum component sweep over the wider window y 1128-1170 found no seventh candidate. Five svarita: 642-654, 1356-1367, 1997-2007, 2299-2309 and 2646-2658, all 11-13 px wide and 33-34 px tall, standing clear above the sirorekha (top edge 1029) with their upper ends at y 993-1007. REJECTED, WITH THE SHAPE REASON. (1) The line-ABOVE (line 4) anudatta band at y 961-975, blobs centred at x 362, 759, 990, 1030, 1255, 1609, 2110, 2312, 2672 and 2790. Rejected because they lie one full line pitch (172 px) above my own bar band and are cut off from my svarita band by rows 976-994, which carry ZERO ink across all 3216 columns. Two are deliberately seductive: x 2312 sits directly above my genuine svarita at 2304, and x 362 directly above my genuine bar at 362. Shape separates them too - they are 35-39 by 11-12 dashes, not 11-13 by 33 strokes. (2) Anusvara dots, rejected as svarita: x 1628-1650 (23 by 25 px, over the ktham of uktham) and x 1881-1901 (21 by 24 px, over the sham of shamsya). Both are round or diamond blobs about as wide as tall, and at 5.9x they are visibly lozenges rather than strokes. This is the discrimination that fixes the fount for me: shamsya carries BOTH a round dot (1891) and an upright stroke (2002) inside one word, so the two glyphs are certainly distinct in this print. (3) Wide curved matras above the headline: 1215-1285 (71 px, the o of sto), 2509-2580 (72 px, the o of so), 2711-2769 (59 px, the long i of pii) and 2851-2911 (61 px, the e of ye). All 59-72 px across and visibly hooked, far wider than the 6-16 px svarita. (4) x 1504-1571, 68 by 2 px at y 1027-1028: the top edge of the sirorekha under the ktha, only two rows tall. Also several one-row slivers at y 1028 (x 347-356, 671-674, 1044-1052, 1156-1159, 1210-1216, 1482-1485), all headline top edge. (5) x 3059-3095, 37 by 22 px at y 1007-1028: the upper lobe of the verse numeral, wider than tall and continuous with the numeral body below the headline. (6) x 3103-3109, 7 by 3 px at y 1124-1126: the tip of the numeral's descending tail. Too small for a bar, above my bar band, and running continuously into the numeral with no white gap. (7) Line 4 curled ink at x 973-1037 y 958-969 and at x 2762-2818 y 958-975: curved hooks and curls (the second is 57 by 18), not straight dashes, and in the line-above band in any case. (8) The subscript ra of the ndra in indraya, a curved hook around x 2284-2322, y 1080-1120: it sits inside my body band, well above the bar band at 1134, and it is a hook rather than a dash. (9) No danda slice contaminates either band. The single danda (x 2107-2124) and the double dandas (2984-3001, 3007-3025, 3142-3181) all lie between the sirorekha and the body floor and never enter y 993-1028 or y 1134-1146. READING PROBLEMS. (a) Word 3 is printed stoma with NO anusvara. Above its final ma there is only the 12 by 34 upright stroke at 1356-1367; at 6.45x there is no round dot, and the 38 px gap to the next word (1384-1421) is completely blank, so no dot sits outside the cluster either. My memory of the Atharvaveda wants stomam here, and in the 1568 px segment I did at first misread this svarita as an anusvara. The ink does not support an anusvara, so I follow the ink: stoma carrying a svarita. (b) unclear_count = 1, namely the first aksara of word 1. At 2024 px I cannot cleanly separate hya (half-ha plus ya) from ha plus an aa-matra: the cluster is 82 px wide (580-661) against 105 px for the sya that follows, and I read the mid-height left spur on its stem as ya, giving hyasya. Either way the mark at x 648 belongs to aksara 0 of that word, so the accent attribution does not depend on the choice. (c) The verse numeral reads 6, a two-lobed figure with a descending tail. I am confident, but it is a single 67 px glyph and I record it as read. (d) Per the fount note I checked the two initial vowels: x 1430-1495 is u (not a), and x 2165-2230 is i. No standalone a occurs on this line, so the ri/shra confusion the note warns about does not arise here.

readers.boundary_interpretation: Word boundaries come from breaks in the sirorekha, read as connected components of the row band y1029-1045: inside a word the headline is unbroken; it stops only at a word space. Headline groups measured in global line-x: 341-534, 575-783, 822-1110, 1149-1383, 1422-1661, 1698-1787, 1828-2065, [2107-2123 = single danda, no headline], 2166-2437, 2472-2922, [2984-2999 and 3007-3023 = double danda, 3052-3097 = numeral, 3143-3180 = double danda, no headline]. Word gaps are 37-52 px wide and cut the headline; aksara boundaries inside a word appear only in the body band (y1046-1110) as 6-22 px white columns with the headline running on above them, so the two kinds of gap are never confusable. Aksara boundaries used (global line-x): word0 e|vaa ~419; word1 ha|sya ~666; word2 kaa|myaa ~949; word3 stoo|ma ~1298; word4 u|kthaM ~1502; word6 shaM|syaa ~1904; word7 i|ndraa ~2230 and ndraa|ya ~2356; word8 soo|ma ~2591, ma|pii ~2673, pii|ta ~2780, ta|ye ~2850. (g) anudatta x1040 in kaamyaa - extent 1021-1059, 72 px right of the kaa|myaa gap (938-959) and directly under the ya stem of the myaa cluster; assigned to myaa. (h) anudatta x1759 - under the one-aksara word ca (body 1699-1780), with 41 px of clear paper to shaMsyaa on the right and 79 px to ukthaM on the left; no alternative carrier. No mark on this line straddles a word gap.
readers.notes: MAGNIFICATION. I started from the two supplied 1568 px segment crops, then rendered my own crops of the same line straight from the leaf JPEG at 2.3x, 2.5x, 2.9x, 4.7x, 5.4x and 7.3x of leaf-block scale, plus binarised versions. The leaf is a 4000 px upscale of a 2024 px master, so a leaf-block pixel is about half a real scan pixel and nothing past ~2.5x adds information; the extra magnification was only for spatial judgement. The decisive evidence is measurement, not viewing: full-width row-ink profiles, per-band 8-connected component extents, and step-1/2/3 ASCII ink maps computed with PIL at thresholds 85, 100, 110, 128, 135, 150 and 170. STABILITY. All eleven marks are present at every threshold from 110 to 170 and no twelfth candidate appears. At thr128 the six bars measure 37, 38, 39, 37, 38, 38 px wide and 11, 11, 12, 11, 10, 10 px tall; the five upright strokes measure 12, 12, 11, 11 and 13 px wide and 32, 32, 31, 31, 31 px tall. Both sets sit squarely inside the shapes the brief describes, and no bar is taller than wide nor any stroke wider than tall. REJECTED FALSE POSITIVES. (1) Ten bars in the y962-975 band, at x362, 759, 989, 1029, 1255, 1609, 2110, 2312, 2672 and 2789. These are line 4's own anudatta bars: one full line pitch (172 px) above my bar band and cut off from my line by the completely blank gutter y976-994. The ones at x2110 and x2312 are the traps - x2110 sits directly above my danda and x2312 directly above indraaya, so at band scale they read as marks on my line. Note also x362, which sits at the same x as one of MY bars, one band up. (2) Four wide curved matras above my headline: x1213-1284 (o of stoo), x2507-2579 (o of soo), x2709-2770 (ii of pii), x2850-2912 (e of ye) - 62 to 73 px across, four to six times too wide for a 6-16 px upright stroke. (3) Two round dots, x1627-1651 (25x28 px) and x1880-1902 (23x23 px): aspect ratio 1.0-1.1, as wide as tall, so anusvara over kthaM and over shaM, not svarita. (4) x3057-3097 above headline level by the verse numeral, 41x22 px: continuous with the numeral body, which runs y1005-1125, so it is the top of the digit, not a free-standing mark. (5) A 59x2 px sliver at x1504-1562, y1025-1026 - the extreme top of the ktha ligature clipped by my band edge. (6) Two flecks: 6x3 px at x2078-2083 y1023-1025 just left of the danda, and 4x3 px at x359-362 y1153-1155 just below my first bar; both under 12 inked pixels, an order of magnitude below any accent. (7) Descenders reaching y1105-1127 at x2214-2245 and x2275-2323 (the i and dra tails of indraaya), x3071-3110 (numeral tail), and the swash tail of word 0's first aksara at x390-416: every one is continuous with its own glyph body with no white gap, so none is a bar. UNRESOLVED 1 of 2. Word 0, aksara 0. The ink is a downward wedge of two short strokes hanging from the headline with a teardrop counter between them (white at x374-388, y1046-1066), merging low into a swash tail that runs down-right to y1112; it has no plain full-height stem reaching the baseline. I read it as e. Reasons: this fount gives its independent vowels swash tails - the i of indraaya does the same, tailing to y1122 - while ordinary consonant stems on this line are plain verticals; and my own unprompted reading of the glyph at low magnification was e, not vocalic-r or shra, which is the misreading the brief's fount note says a provokes. I still record it as unclear, because on silhouette alone a cannot be excluded and the fount note may be aimed at exactly this glyph. The accent is unaffected either way: the bar at x362 belongs to this aksara. UNRESOLVED 2 of 2. Word 1, aksara 0. The ink shows a single consonant here, not a conjunct. Its body is 79 px wide (x582-660), the same as the single consonant ca (x1699-1780, 82 px), whereas every consonant-plus-ya conjunct on this line is 114-120 px wide (sya at x670-783 is 114 px; the m+ya of kaamyaa is 120 px), because this fount always writes ya with its own crescent counter and its own stem. This glyph has no ya element, and there is no ink at all below y1112 beneath it, so there is no stacked subscript either. On shape - upper-left curve, lower-left loop, a hook descending down-right, and a plain right stem at x642-660 - I read ha, giving hasya. I record it unclear because a reader who knows the corpus will expect hyasya here and I cannot formally exclude an unusually narrow hya ligature; but the width evidence is against it and, per the brief, I have followed the ink rather than the expectation. The accent is unaffected: svarita on this aksara, anudatta on sya. The verse numeral I read as 6 - a top hook, an S-curve, a lower-right loop and a descending tail, y1005-1125; 5, 8 and 9 do not fit the silhouette, but I hold this at moderate confidence only, and it is not an aksara so it is not counted in unclear_count. All coordinates here are leaf-text-block x, which is the brief's global line-x (block width 3216); I measured the source image directly rather than converting from the rendered crops, so no 0.9469 rescale was applied.

readers.notes: MAGNIFICATION: the two supplied 1568px segments, then my own 4-segment crops from scripts/crop_atharvaveda_line.py, then my own PIL crops of single aksaras at 5x-13x, and finally direct measurement of the leaf jpg (row and column ink profiles, connected-run extents and ASCII ink maps at thresholds 128 and 150). Every accept or reject below is from the measurements; the crops only served to name letters. REJECTED FALSE POSITIVES. (1) Ten dashes at x344-381, 740-778, 973-1007, 1024-1036, 1237-1274, 1591-1628, 2092-2129, 2294-2331, 2653-2691, plus a 57x18 curl at 2762-2818: all lie in y962-974, one full line pitch (172px) above my own bar band, so they are line 4's anudatta layer. Two of them are almost exactly column-aligned with marks of mine - 2294-2331 over my svarita at 2299-2309, and 2653-2691 over my svarita at 2646-2658 - which is the trap the brief names; the y band, not the x, decided them. (2) Wide curved matras above my own headline, rejected on width: 1215-1283 (69px, the o of sto), 2509-2576 (68px, the o of so), 2851-2911 (61px, the e of ye), and 2711-2767 (57px wide, 29 tall, the i-matra arch of pi - one connected arch whose two legs run down into the sirorekha, not a narrow stroke). (3) Two round lens-shaped blobs above the headline, 1628-1650 (23x25) and 1881-1901 (21x23): about as wide as tall and tapering to points at top and bottom, i.e. the anusvara of uktham and of samsya, not upright strokes. For contrast, my five accepted svaritas are all 11-13px wide and 32-33 rows tall. (4) A 40x21 round blob with a stem at 3059-3095: the upper loop of the verse numeral, not a mark. (5) Two runs only 1 row tall at 1506-1528 and 1543-1557 in the upper-band scan: the top fringe of my own sirorekha at y1028, not marks. (6) Below the line no candidate was a vocalic-r hook or a halanta tail: all six bars are 37-39px wide and 10-12px tall, wider than tall, and sit isolated in y1134-1146 with zero ink in y1127-1133, so none of them touches a descender, and none is a danda slice (no ink leaves the band at either end). READ AGAINST MY FIRST INSTINCT - the one unclear aksara: the first cell of word 1 (x578-662). At high magnification it reads to a modern eye like 'ha with something subjoined', and my memory wanted hy-asya. The ink does not support ha. I found a certain ha on this same leaf (line 6, x2256-2313, in the word ending -him) and measured it: this fount's ha is only 58px wide and is a pure curl with NO full-height right vertical - its right side breaks off partway down. My glyph is 83px wide and carries a 23px vertical that hangs from the sirorekha at x640-662 and runs unbroken to y1109. I also excluded ka (x829-907 on this same line): ka is solid at the top and splits at the bottom, the inverse of my glyph. My glyph's skeleton is: an upper-left curl separated from a full-height right stem by a white channel at x630-638 that persists from y1047 to y1074; a solid crossbar y1075-1091 joining curl to stem; then a lower-left curl that leaves the body at y1096 and sweeps down-right from x594 to x634, ending below the baseline at y1111. That is the skeleton of Devanagari a (U+0905), and its descending lower curl is exactly what the brief's fount note describes as reading like vocalic-r or shra. So I read the word as a-sya and counted 1 unclear aksara. The accent attribution is unaffected either way: the svarita stands over that first cell and the anudatta under the second. The verse numeral was confirmed as 6 by comparing it with the numerals that close lines 3 and 4 of the same leaf (4 and 5, so the sequence runs 4, 5, 6) and with the '61' at the head of line 6, which uses the identical sort. Nothing else on the line was doubtful.
